plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for IgniteNet MetroLinq 60 GHz radios (enterprise PEN 47307, IGNITENET-MIB). Besides standard IF-MIB interface traffic and uptime, it reports per-radio transmit power, local and remote RSSI and whether the 60 GHz link has failed over to the 5 GHz radio.
name: Wireless

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: ignitenet_radio_tx_power_dbm
metrics.description: Per-radio transmit power in dBm from IGNITENET-MIB mlRadioInfoTxPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.47307.1.4.2.1.7), stored as the raw Integer32 with no scaling. Values outside -40..60 dBm are dropped.

metrics.name: ignitenet_radio_rssi_local
metrics.description: RSSI value reported by the radio for the local site from IGNITENET-MIB mlRadioInfoRSSILocal (1.3.6.1.4.1.47307.1.4.2.1.10). The MIB does not specify its unit; the raw Integer32 is stored with no scaling.

metrics.name: ignitenet_radio_rssi_remote
metrics.description: RSSI value reported by the radio for the remote site from IGNITENET-MIB mlRadioInfoRSSIRemote (1.3.6.1.4.1.47307.1.4.2.1.11). The MIB does not specify its unit; the raw Integer32 is stored with no scaling.

metrics.name: ignitenet_radio_failover_state
metrics.description: Whether the 60 GHz radio has failed over to the 5 GHz radio, from IGNITENET-MIB mlRadioStatusFailoverStatus (1.3.6.1.4.1.47307.1.4.3.1.2). off(0) maps to 1 (normal) and on(1) maps to 2 (abnormal); other values are dropped.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
